am.bidari-guli.about: An interpretive Bidri (Bidriware) setting: Alaguli Mane played on a blackened-brass mancala tray inlaid with project-original silver medallions, star work, and floral forms.
am.bidari-guli.attribution.board: Project-original Bidri-style blackened-brass and silver mancala-board artwork.
am.bidari-guli.attribution.table: Project-original Bidri-style seamless silver-diaper tabletop tile.
am.bidari-guli.claim.bidri: Bidri (Bidriware) is a documented metal-inlay craft of Bidar, Karnataka — blackened white-brass with pure-silver inlay — geographical-indication registered in 2006.
am.bidari-guli.claim.interpretive: The black-metal-and-silver look is an artistic homage; this mancala tray is not an authentic Bidriware object and no historical claim is made that Alaguli Mane used Bidri boards.
am.bidari-guli.disclosure.interpretive: Bidari Guli is a digital homage in the Bidri idiom. It uses no protected emblem, no copied artisan motif, and implies no real silver or endangered material.
am.bidari-guli.intent: Count every seed across the silver-ringed pits and plan the next sowing chain.
am.bidari-guli.teaching.capture-1: Four seeds gather into the store, bright against blackened brass; count the next sowing chain before lifting a pit.
am.bidari-guli.teaching.lose-1: The other store holds the larger harvest; trace the silver pits one relay further next time.
am.bidari-guli.teaching.win-1: The fuller store carries the harvest after patient counting, seed by seed across the silver inlay.
am.bidari-guli.title: Bidari Guli — Bidri Pits
